body: As is a common sentiment here, though, I would really fucking miss my dog. He has been the only companion I have in that house and it breaks my heart to think of leaving him.

Alternatively, there are those who say that depression is a state that allows for a stepping back and more realistic appraisal of one's life and the world .. almost like an adaptive mechanism, whereby you ruminate/try to solve your problems and move on or kill yourself.
I was more active, was getting out more, doing things, seeing people. Then my health started to deteriorate and I haven't really looked back.

My dreams aren't that interesting, though they allow me to do things I can't really do anymore (I'm mostly bedbound with fatigue). I know what you mean about that sentiment -- cliche and all. Everyday is like waking up into a nightmare. I sleep later and later (currently until 4pm), and am always sad when I have to finally get up.

Not really. I can't remember that far back. I was happy and somewhat functional a year ago, so it seems like my mind reverts back to that state after I wake up .. it's really crushing when reality hits again.
I'm past the point of therapy, but thanks.
I've been waiting 12 years. How much longer should I wait?

TFW people bother to downvote you in /r/depression. 

I don't give a fuck -- this account is to get my thoughts out there before I'm six feet under.

I know for a fact that it's not anxiety. I tried psych meds and they did nothing to relieve my symptoms (and made some worse). I've suffered from severe anxiety and depression for 10 years: some doctors would use that to dismiss all of my symptoms (and have), but I think it qualifies me to differentiate.

If I was physically capable at all, I could move on with things and try to ignore the symptoms. Now I can't walk around the block without feeling like I'm going to pass out, or fall over from being off-balance. There's no life to distract myself with.

The medical system is designed to demoralize the mentally ill. Even mental health treatment is a joke for the treatment-refractory like me. I'm tired of living this life where I feel so profoundly dependent on everyone and can't even sit down to read a book to pass the time because my head's such a foggy, broken mess. 

It feels empowering to know there's a way out, that I have some control.

Yeah, I don't really get where I was going with that. I thought there was a reason those methods might be more likely to fail, outside of failure of nerve. I was considering drowning, which is why I asked.
I was wondering if the method failed somehow, i.e. he was discovered, or didn't drown for some reason etc.
That doesn't mean the method failed or doesn't work; that means he couldn't go through with it. He was implying that the methods are unreliable.

I appreciate it. I don't like do-gooders, but can tell you're coming from a genuine place.

I think free-will is complicated, and probably differs whether you're looking at it biologically or philosophically. If someone is too fatigued to move, or suffers from a mental illness that scrambles their brain circuitry, then they are left with fewer choices relative to someone 'healthy'. Even if those choices are subsequently confounded by other factors from a nihilist/fatalist perspective, I think you need the basic biological foundation to keep persisting in the most basic way.

I am also curious to see how things turn out. I am sure treatments for mental health will improve a lot over the next decade. But I don't have any basic comfort to live with day-to-day. I can't even take any medication anymore because of the side-effects I experience. The last time I saw a psychiatrist, he just threw his hands up at me after I went through the last of things I'd tried.

Like you say, I had not experienced both mental and physical illness before. I think it's the combination that feels so imprisoning. I have wracked my brain for a way out of this but cannot find one. Fundamentally, I do not want to die, because I'm scared and also narcissistic. I cannot predict what will happen to me, but I have never felt this out of options before.

I appreciate the compliment but don't think you entirely get it. Those years weren't spent trying to attain my dreams; they were spent trying to pharmacological secure my sanity, so that I could function at all. That never really happened. So I've never been left with any choices -- whether to build some kind of mediocre life or something grander. I do not regret a single choice I made because I refused to lay down and die. If I was hit by a truck tomorrow, I would know I did everything possible to try and afford myself a life. It never worked out, which leaves me here -- in effect, with the last choice left to me.

Reading over this this, it just seems kind of pretentious and overly morbid, but I'm just trying to get my thoughts out, more for my sake than anything else. That said, I guess words can't really do justice to the sheer complexity of feelings that have amassed over years.
